chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi from Marwan ibn Muslim from Abu al-Hasan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
My father differed with the people regarding the wealth of the orphan; there is no zakat upon it.
ai.seo_question: Is zakat obligatory on the wealth of orphans according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the juristic distinction held by Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that zakat is not obligatory on the capital wealth of orphans, differing from the general consensus which often extends zakat obligations to children's assets. This view underscores the principle that zakat is a purification of surplus wealth acquired through trade or growth, which may not apply in the same manner to the preserved principal of a minor. The report is recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, reflecting the nuanced legal reasoning within the Shia tradition regarding the financial status of minors.
